reviews.review_msg: Barry is a funny guy, but extremely boring as a professor. He does not even seem interested in what he is teaching so how can anyone else be? Really did not enjoy this class, especially when Hilary Morden was my TA. Hugest nightmare of my life.

One of the more demanding core courses with 1 short paper and 2 - 8 page papers. Your mark depends on who your TA is, since they are marking your paper. The presentation/participation marks are easy marks.  His final is just like his other exams; and read the articles and pay attention to the movie he plays.
tries to make a boring subject entertaining with his powerpoints. good prof and a fair amount of assignments.

gotta put in a lot of work for this class. 2 8page papers marked pretty hard. final was pretty easy compared to all the course work. overall very dry material, barry tries to make it interesting. difficult class but will do fine if you put in the effort. make sure to get a good TA for the class though

Have had this course for crim 300 and 104. His text are easy just re-right notes he gives but papers are tough so got to the ta before you hand in to make corrections before you get a back mark. Enjoyed his classes

Everything mentioned in the final exam review class is on the exam. With a written take home midterm, term paper, presentation, and final, was a lot of work for little payoff (20% per component). Presentation and participation were too highly weighted IMO. Grade (except for final) depends on TA. Wish there was more overlap of lecture and readings.

CRIM 300 is a writing intensive course, which scared me at first, but the way he had divided the total mark for class made it possible to compensate if you dont do well once. TA was hard on marking though, which made me a better writer!! GO to lecture though, if you dont you miss a lot
What can I say? This guy is the best prof at SFU and everyone should experience life w/ Barry at some point in time.  Great prof, easy exams, interesting lectures, great guy!
Lecture notes are posted online, but there is still a LOT of note taking. Marking and exams are fair. Lectures can be rather boring though.
Awesome Prof! Theory can be pretty boring, but Barry manages to make lectures interesting and entertaining.

This was my 3rd class with Barry at SFU - he's one of the best professors I've ever had. Highly recommended! Very helpful, highly respectful towards his students. Asks us for future suggestions to improve his teaching tactics. Good sense of humor - fair marking, fair assignments. Finally, a professor who knows how to teach :)

It's fine... Depends on the TA but I would complain that the modules are hard to navigate and incomplete.
Turnaround for marking isn't fast but isn't absurdly slow. There is lots of annotation returned to you. Marking is very very nitpicky. 
Sometimes the lecture recording and module instructions differ.

The online design of this class is fine, and the workload is manageable. The course is what you expect for a required upper-div course on theory. BUT Dr. Faubert herself is very difficult to communicate with. She lives in another province so email is the only way, and she is not good at it. She's short, dismissive, and disinterested. AVOID her.
not a fair marker at all! super boring too.

I honestly expected this course to be super difficult but Jacqueline made it as easy as possible. If you follow the guidelines and do basically everything thats required with some effort, achieving a B or anything higher is easily doable! Jacqueline is easily the best prof for online courses, also had her for 321 online. 10/10 would recommend!

Tough, but fair. Class consists of weekly Canvas discussions (10%), a 2 - 3 page presentation (5%), two BBC discussions (10%), and three 8 - 10 page papers (75%). Expects a lot from students, but gives excellent feedback on the papers to help you improve each time. Not overly writing intensive compared to what others make it seem. Highly recommend
bad marker

Took two classes with her, crim 300 and 321 and both were great! TA's were awesome and participation marks are great mark boosters. Papers for crim 300 were tough, 321 was good because she didnt require you to do the research. Final exam was easy! All written.

Good distance ed. class. Papers require efforts. Final exam is easy-to-do. TA seems to be helpful. The online participation and presentation are point grabbers so do well in them to bump up your marks.
Jacqueline is awesome! She is extremely helpful and encourages students to do well in the class by taking the time to post comments & feedback. Would definitely take another class w/ her again!
Had her for 230 last semester and she is AWESOME! very interesting...very engaging...VERY sad to see her go... =(

she makes theory INTERESTING! I KNOW! i didnt think that was possible either! but the way she applies it to real life, it kind of makes you think abt theory in a whole new light. and come to think of it, we use theory everyday in our lives, we just dont realize it. love her course, would and am taking her again.

She tries to make the material as interesting as possible. She loves what she's doing and is passionate about what she's teaching.  She's a good speaker, but can get a little dry sometimes. The workload is very manageable and she marks pretty easily.

Faubert tries her best to make the material interesting and easy to learn, which is all but impossible...Theory just sucks! She has everything going against her and yet she is personable, interested and helpful. Would take another class with her again.

Great prof. Very nice & approachable. The 2 papers are very easy, I didn't read the text, and did very well in the class. But make sure you listen in LEC, so you know what's going on. LEC is quite boring though. I would take Faubert again. 7/10.
She's a good prof, a little boring, but livable.
Theory class so she has that going against her. Lectures were a little boring but in a smaller format class like crime 452- very interesting and very approachable. Takes the time to get to know you.
Give her chocolate pudding before your exam
great prof. the class was a bore but her assignments were straightforward
she's very nice & helpful. she knows the crim theories well but her lectures are boring. this class is all about application of crim theories in papers.
Makes the theory class as good as it can get.  Unfortunately, it is still boring, but hey, it's a prereq!  A very pleasant, down-to-earth and easy to deal with person.  She will make time for you.

Well... it IS a theory course, but that aside it was tolerable and Jackie is a great lecturer, very receptive to questions and comments during lecture, and knows it forwards, backwards and inside out.
She is very thorough in her lectures..but lectures exact same as notes received from WebCT. Material is difficult, and assignments are kind of hard too. Work hard and u should be fine.
Jackie is one of the best prof's I have ever had. She is very fair and objective.  She makes theory fun and interesting.  Definately take this class with her, you will not be dissapointed.
She does an awesome job of trying to make theory interesting. Very good prof, highly recommend that you take this course with her cause theory can be SO boring.
She is an AWESOME teacher and she is very clear, fair minded, and tolerant of everybodys opinion

She loves criminology! She is extremely helpfull, and you get the impression that she can't wait to mark your paper. Best teacher ever to go see in office hours! She is the type of teacher that most departments could only dream of.

I like the fact that she is not bias and she explains all theories without promoting ones she likes and dissing ones she doesn't like.  She sticks to the facts and keeps her personal opinions out of class
She is an AMAZING teacher!  You actually leave her classes feeling as if you have learnt something!
Great prof, organized, knowledgeble and fair. Exams were fair and within my expectations

Jacky is a great prof. Her tests are very fair. She tests you on what you know rather than what you don't know. Partial lecture notes can be printed from WebCT. The material was interesting. Some of the articles were difficult to understand though.
she's so cool ... reminds me of my buddy's mom
she is really nice and makes sense

Super helpful and supportive. Leads interesting discussions. Hard marker but provides great feadback to improve and this course was structured so that there were many assingments and opportunities to make up for bad marks. Great TA over all.

she's tough but very fair. is helpful when you need her help. if you follow the guidelines set out by the professor and do everything you're supposed to with a decent amount of effort. as long as you speak at least twice every class, you will get full participation marks. it's possible to participate w/o reading assigned readings.

Good luck on the final, 9-12 pages in 1.5 hours. personally, my TA was not helpful and frequently said opposite things of the rubrics and course material. It's a writing course but no actual guidance on how to write well. Expectations of a 4th year, outlines of a 1st year.
difficult class,TA's are also not good at communicating and do not show up to office hours, assignments were tough (I dreaded doing each one), please take CRIM30W with another professor

Honestly I was scared looking at the reviews but class was not bad. Had Janine as my TA, absolute best. She always clarified and provided amazing feedback. Prof's lectures were interesting/informational. End of term test was kind of surprising and difficult - the theories tested were not common theories. Midterm paper 8-10 pages + final paper 12-15
great class if you like crying during a final
u could do good in the whole class and here comes the final to knock u down
Brutal final
you guys…what was that final exam…i'm so mind bLOWN at how atrocious it is omg… we better be CURVED

didn't go to a single lecture, put in minimal effort and got a B+. Very easy class, just grind out a couple papers on the day its due and u can forget about this class for the rest of the semester. other than tutorial participation which was whatever

Dr. Lysova's class was a breath of fresh air. I found applying theories to real-life scenarios incredibly engaging. Dr. Lysova's encouragement of critical thinking and objectivity made her an exceptional instructor.
Professor Lysova's lectures provide insight into contemporary issues relating to social behaviours and criminality. Highly recommended!

Dr. Lysova's course completely changed my perspective. Applying theories to everyday situations felt so natural by the end. I'm grateful for Dr. Lysova's emphasis on critical thinking; it was truly valuable. Her teaching style, which was both objective and creative, made her stand out as an excellent professor.

Nice prof but there are major areas where she can improve:

1. Communicate with TAs better because it leads to miscommunication and it was present during the course.

2. A final exam where we're given 2 hours to write 3 essays (6 pages each) being graded on grammar, isn't too realistic.

3. Be present since during the final exam, she wasn't there.
The best professor at SFU. Dr. Lysova is highly educated, knowledgeable, passionate, and kind. Also, she did her best to support us during the strike.

I enjoyed this class. Although lectures were not mandatory, they were informative and helped understand difficult concepts. Case studies and examples were interesting and helpful. Tutorial participation mattered.

Lectures were pretty useless for this course since the two papers you have to write were just based on the textbook, however, attendance for tutorials was mandatory since it's worth a significant portion of your grade. Overall, the course itself was not difficult but the papers did feel repetitive as they were pretty much about the same topic.

No exams which made lectures very optional (went to first 2 and that was it). You have to write 2 papers and submit outlines a couple weeks before the real thing is due. They're long ones (10-15 pages each) but the topics are relatively easy to write a lot about. Tutorial participation is worth like 25% so its important u show up and participate.

You really don't need to go to the boring lectures because assignments can be done with the readings only. Assignments are not too hard if you listen exactly to what they are asking and they give clear instructions. For tutorial make sure you show up, raise questions, and engage in the material to deepen the discussion and you'll get marked fairly

There were only 2 assignments: a midterm and final paper, 8 and 12 pages respectively. Participation in tutorials was kinda bad because you had to read some random research study and talk about it for tutorial on top of the textbook and it was worth a lot. My TA wasn't clear on the rubric and lots of people ended up really low in a grade worth 30%

Her 300W course isn't as bad as 313, because you're not expected to read hundreds of pages of some geriatric boomer's opinions. Also, the lectures are relevant and while not necessary to attend, can at least help you understand the course content better. Also, Kayleigh was helpful and accessible outside of class. Definitely a tough grader though.
This class went smoothly online and I enjoyed all of the content during this course. Lots of feedback on the drafts was helpful and made me feel more comfortable with writing.

The papers for this class are unnecessarily difficult. You are required to write 15 pages for the final paper with a whopping 21 required sources cited, 15 of which must be academic journal articles. The due date for the good copy is rendered void by the draft (completed in full) which is due 3 weeks prior. Class was basically taught by the TA.
The final exam expected 3500-4000 words for five long answer essay questions in three hours. Pretty unrealistic and needlessly stressful. Thanks. Okay lecturer but change your course formatting.

Terrible final. 3 hours to write 5 questions didnt sound too terrible until you realized she wanted 3500-4000 words ... other than that this class was great. TAs mark everything, I lucked out with Kayleigh, she was accommodating and easy to understand (unlike mass emails from Ryan) I hope they change expectations for the final in the future
Your exam and paper grades will depend on your TA at least that's how it was last sem. However, it is not a difficult class at all.
Thanks to you people who never went to lecture she does not post lecture slides anymore

Barely went to lecture as Dr. Lysova often went on tangents and would go very fast through her slides. However she does post her slides so you can review them on your own. Make sure you follow your TA's expectations as there were different expectations. Final exam was very fair. Save yourself some money and dont buy the textbook.

Alexandra is knowledgeable in her field. Although the class was dry and about theories, she tried to engage students. Her notes were easy to read and she was always encouraged questions from students. Great prof. She is easy to get ahold of and is caring prof outside of the classrooms
Excellent lectures. Really enthusiastic about class content. I really liked it. Also very happy that she expanded the info beyond what the text said. Great professor!
Professor Lysova has a lot of energy and does a great job of keeping us focused and interested in the class. I really enjoyed this class, especially for an 8:30 am one! :)

Alexandra was very knowledgeable and passionate about the course material, which made the learning environment enjoyable. She was always helpful and clarified any questions or concerns. Overall great professor!

It's a mandatory class and she seems to be the only one teaching it recently... seems to love the biological perspectives of crime? Doesn't post slides online and zooms through things that aren't in the textbook and cannot be found anywhere... likes to show movies and video clips, criteria on syllabus completely changed by TA's for assignments >:(
She is super helpful and  approachable! One of the best TA!
Considering this is a writing intensive course, Asheka is a pretty easy marker. Didn't really learn anything new but I would much rather take an easy marker over some of the other crazy TA's at SFU.

Barry is an interesting character, I still do not find him as entertaining as others.  The TA does all of the marking and the marking scheme is well laid out.  I found Aimee (TA) to be quite nice although she may look unapproachable, if you have a problem she will help you out, you just have to try and approach her.

Very fun lecturer, and I couldn't complain. The material was interesting and relevant. The essays were easy if you did the readings. Why do so many people dislike Amy? She's a good TA, just strict about plagiarism. If you follow the most recent form of APA, and take her advice to heart, she won't deduct marks. I think you're all patch-writers.

I liked Barry.  He was entertaining (though mildly inappropriate) and very approachable.  The TA, Aimee Smith, on the other hand had some rather interesting ideas on APA format and tended to focus her marking on her own skewed perception of the format.  Still got an A, but the lady needs to take a refresher course.

its a writing course so there were a lot of papers. The midterm was a take home essay which i found beneficial=) he keeps his lectures interesting and he's pretty funny. Good ppt but you need to attend lectures because he post partial sections online so you have to come lol. Be prepared to write and read critically its not just a slack class

very predictable and straight forward with exams and papers. a presentation and participation are worth a lot and bump up your mark. does powerpoint notes that are pretty much the textbook--so u don't need to do the readings. plus, a really helpful and nice guy.

Dave was an awesome teacher, but I've never heard of him giving anything higher than an A- (and very few of those too!). Still, he was very helpful and extremely committed to the students/course. He does expect you to work hard though!

Class was based on tutorials, major paper and a final, there was no midterm. Major assignment was okay.. but final was hard. Cumulative and heavy content, over 100 marks. Dawn is nice, she tries to help her students but it is a very content heavy class and you should attend lectures even though they are recorded.

Rault kept the lectures engaging and often allowed for significant in-lecture participation. The class consisted of an annotated bib, major paper, tutorial participation, reflection assignment, and a final exam. Be sure to keep up on the readings and go to tutorial as they help a lot!! The final was a little difficult IMO so review lecture and text
One of the best prof's. Hard marker but extra caring. Dont judge her yet (in the middle of the semester), wait until the end. You'll be surprised!

She's a great professor and cares about her students. Yes you have to put in the work, two large essays and four thought papers. The thought papers are easy. She made the class interesting. She offers bonus marks and she isn't there to screw us over she tells you exactly what she wants. SFU needs more professors like her!

People who don't like Hilary and her teaching style really need to grow up/actually put in effort. As a fourth year I've fully enjoyed taking this WRITING INTENSIVE class with her. She is so helpful and offers chances for bonus and will take the best of the 2 term papers as your grade. She's even making the final optional for grade improvement

Hilary is a great teacher! She is interesting to listen to and is passionate about Crim. She is a no bs person, if you don't put the effort in she wont put the effort into you. I would take her again.

I took this last spring, and my marks have improved immensely (B+ to A+). Hilary actually takes time to criticize your work, other TAs don't. You can't LEARN unless u accept your flaws. If you want to learn, she is super helpful. If you want to cruise through uni w/out academic improvement, then suit yourself -- she's not easy, but she is the best.

Yes, she's hard - but really fair.  She stayed extra hours for office hours and was willing to go through my essay line by line to help me with my writing.  My essay marks have gone up a full grade since. She is focused on helping students to achieve the very best possible.
STAY AWAY AT ALL TIMES. WORST TA I'VE EVER HAD. She will say your essay is wrong from top to bottom
HORRIBLE TA. STAY AWAY FROM HER. Not useful. Only focuses on wrong APA practices. Doesn't even discuss about the paper content. She's horrible.
Really good instructor! I enjoyed this class thoroughly. He is very passionate about criminology and always made an 8.30 class interesting! Fair expectations, fair marking, easy-going!

need the textbook, entire class is based on empirical evidence and theories.  This prof loves to see empirical evidence in exams and essays. he marks hard. writing intensive. he likes to see main concepts from theories combined with your critical thinking with empirical evidence to support or refute arguments made.
oops last post had a typo. had him fall 07..not 08!

Had Jon as a TA fall 08. great TA! was very helpful. always available to go over papers and questions about exams. very fair marker. serious students (i.e., non-slackers) will appreciate his interest and knowledge about crim theories.
Awesome TA, extremely helpful, and fair marker.

One of my favourite profs at SFU. Lectures are actually fun. He makes the content so straightforward and easy to memorize. Exams are manageable - 4-5 essay questions and you write how much you want, and lots of freedom with the paper. There was also a tutorial group presentation, but easy A

I like logan a lot as a professor. He makes the lectures very engaging and interesting. I like the format of this class too. Studying for the tests are quite easy as he brings the material from the powerpoints which has all the info. Overall I would take his class again.

He is great! His lectures are super engaging and he goes into detail about each theory to ensure that we understand. His exams are only a few questions and you write however much you think you need to in order to get your point across. The only bad thing is it takes him about a week to post lecture slides. I definitely recommend taking his class!
Great guy, best TA ever.
Helpful, nice, and funny. One of the best TA's I've had. Has weird hair but hot.
Had him for a TA. Awesome guy, would take again.
Tried to make uninteresting material bearable.

She's the most down to earth, friendly and helpful person I've met. She's smart and really encouraging. I think she has qualities that other profs are sorely lacking. I hope I get her in a seminar or something.

I had Ryan as a TA for both crim 300w and crim 317. He comes across as a little intimidating at first, but is actually really hilarious and caring. I felt that he had high expectations, but went out of his way to provide tons of feedback on assignments. He also tries to make course content applicable to real life settings. Would highly recommend!

One of my fav classes in my degree. I love her teaching style, and her enthusiasm that always brought me excited to her lectures. She spent so much time with me helping me edit my papers and answering all of my questions. My writing improved so much with her guidance. Tough class but follow her feedback and go to office hours, and you'll do great.

Sarah was an amazing prof. I went into this class struggling to write a compeling an good paper. I ended up getting a really bad grade on my proposal but she worked with me to better my writing skills to the point where I felt confident handing in my finals draft. Her lectures are inspiring and she is engaging with students.
Avoid if you can.. Tough marker and super high expectations.. Yes university is not supposed to be easy, but this was the hardest class - cause of the prof out of the 15+ courses I've taken.
The class was unorganized and guidelines were not clear.

Professional & prepared. thorough guidelines but lengthy. Knows what she's talking about, helpful in emails & office hours. Prof Y was always quick to respond to me, let me come to office hours for a different class when I couldnt make it on mondays. Grading was tough but reasonable & I think she bumped in the end.

Prof took the time to meet with me and work through any questions. Wish I took this class before the end of my uni. Very passionate about what she teaches and knowledgeable too. Clearly knew her stuff and made it relatable and easy to understand too. Very accessible, approachable and a great teacher. BUT the TA was disconnected and mean.

Sarah is hands down the best prof I have had at SFU. She is kind, and passionate about the topics she lectures on. The course material for 300 is dull but Sarah made the class entertaining. Highly recommend!

Not an easy a but if you work for it you will be rewarded. Fair and reasonable grading and impressive amounts of feedback. Gives students opportunities to improve their grades. Great person and lecturer. She kept class interesting and funny and is also very kind and approachable. Yerchcih makes a notoriously tough class (300) good.
Worst prof at sfu.

Not the class you want to take if you have extra curricular commitments, like a job.   Assigns work like it's the only class are taking this semester.  A little condescending. For example, a student asked a relevant question during lecture and she told him to look it up bc it was the best way to learn.  Rude.
This is a writing class so there's a lot of writing. Don't take it thinking you won't write cuz you will. A lot. Tough class but goodfair prof.

Sarah's class was what I would expect from any university class. She was sweet (when one-on-one) and helpful, but strict and demanding. Her class wasn't easy, but it didn't make me bleed. She even gave us an extension on a paper. But her 'take home midterm' was brutal (I know, it sounds like a breeze right??).

Amazing TA! Gave great detailed feedback and was always happy to help.  I have never had a TA care as much about helping me learn before. Understands and explains theory well! Gives good feedback. I would take a class with her again.
Awesome TA! Helpful and interesting. Detailed marks on papers and exams helped me to learn.  Always made time to meet with me or e-mail me with assistance. Always cheerful and friendly. Love her!

A professor who genuinely cares for her students. Her instructions and marking criteria are clear, all you need is to FOLLOW THEM and you will likely be rewarded with a good grade. Don't fear the drafts for the papers, they are meant to prevent you from procrastination and keep you on track. Trust me, you will be very thankful for them later.
Goes off topic quite often but will rush through in the last 15 minutes. Rubric is detailed, strict prof, cry now.

Tamie is one of the best professors Ive had. She's caring, gives really informative lectures, and really wants her students to do well. The only thing that irked me were the milestone papers as they collided with assignments for my other classes and stressed me, but if time is prioritized right, its such a helpful tool that makes your work better.

Very straightforward lectures that provide clear expectations for what she's looking for in the assignments. Since this was a W class there was an outline, bibliography and term paper to submit which were all very doable and she offered examples to follow. No complaints whatsoever, and TA Kelley was great, accessible for help and gave good feedback

The course was self-directed with a few quizzes, assignments, and a term paper. The assignment outlines were unclear, lectures & slides were unorganized, and going to campus for tutorial or lecture were not a good use of time. The course did not teach me anything new or important. Regardless, Dr. Spicer is understanding and nice.
Dr Spicer is fantastic!!!!!! Helpful, kind, passionate, and is clear in regards to what she expects from her students. Not too easy, not too hard. Highly recommend!
Very nice prof that really cares about her students.
